title: Which Way? Cross Product Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Twist a bottle cap and it rises. Turn a screw and it sinks in. When Aarav pushes his spanner sideways, the bolt does not move sideways at all: it goes straight in, at right angles to both the spanner and his push. Why that way? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn the vector (cross) product.

On a live motion notebook vector B turns around vector A on a flat floor while A x B grows, shrinks and flips below the floor, the readout tracks theta, sin theta and A x B, and a graph traces the sine curve. The size always equals the shaded parallelogram. A slow-mo replay freezes at 30 degrees to measure the area and use the right-hand rule, and we swap the order to see why B x A = -A x B. Then the unit vector rules step by step (i x j = k round the circle), the spanner link by link, the dot product and the cross product side by side, and a worked example on graph paper. Then the exam trap (i x k is minus j), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.

In this video:
0:00 Why does the bolt go straight in?
0:25 Size, direction and the right-hand rule
0:49 Motion notebook: turn B around A
1:25 Slow-mo replay: area at 30 degrees
1:41 Pause and think: B x A
1:57 Unit vectors in four steps
2:37 The spanner, link by link
3:01 Dot vs cross + pause and think
3:34 Worked example: area on graph paper
4:08 Exam trap: i x k
4:29 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:07 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Angular Velocity and Linear Velocity. On a merry-go-round all the horses turn together, yet the outer horse travels faster. How?
